Severity ratings use likelihood x impact with stated reasons. Uses the report format.

evals.expected_output: Reports that the export route now bypasses requireAuth: it is registered on app before the /api router, so the middleware never runs and any unauthenticated visitor can download any report by iterating integer IDs (missing authentication, CWE-306; OWASP A07:2025 or A01:2025 / API2 or API5:2023). Notes this comes from walking the entry points (Pass B), not from a data-flow trace, and that the bug is in what the diff moved rather than in any changed line of the handler. Severity is Critical or High with Likelihood High (unauthenticated, one request, enumerable IDs) × Impact High (every customer's report). Also reports, as a separate pre-existing issue, that exportReport has no ownership or account filter even when authenticated (IDOR, CWE-639), and flags that CDN caching of per-customer data is itself an exposure risk (cache key and Cache-Control). Fix: keep the route on the authenticated router, scope the lookup to the caller's account, and send Cache-Control: private, no-store (or cache per user only with a signed, expiring URL). Regression test: an unauthenticated request to the export route gets 401.
expectations: Reports that the export route is registered on app before the /api router, so requireAuth never runs and anyone can download any report

evals.prompt:
Can you check this new GitHub Actions workflow for security problems? It builds a preview site for every PR, including PRs from forks.

```yaml
name: PR preview
on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize]
permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm ci && npm run build
        env:
          PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
      - run: echo "Built preview for: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"
      - run: ./scripts/deploy-preview.sh
        env:
          PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN }}
```
evals.expected_output: Treats the workflow as reachable by anyone who can open a fork PR, and does not demote it as build tooling. Reports two findings. (1) Critical: pull_request_target checks out and runs the PR head (npm ci runs the PR's install scripts; npm run build and deploy-preview.sh are attacker-controlled) with the deploy secret in the environment and a contents: write token, so any GitHub user can steal the secret and push to the repository. (2) High or Critical: script injection, because the PR title is interpolated with ${{ }} directly into a run step, so a title containing shell syntax executes in a privileged job. Fixes: build untrusted code under the pull_request trigger with no secrets and a read-only token, and deploy from a separate workflow_run job that never executes PR code; pass the title through an env variable and quote it; set least-privilege permissions per job. Notes action pinning to a commit SHA as hardening. Uses the report format with likelihood × impact reasoning.
expectations: Treats the workflow as reachable by anyone who can open a fork PR
Reports as critical that pull_request_target checks out and runs the PR head with the deploy secret and a write token
Reports the PR title interpolated with ${{ }} into a run step as script injection, rated high or critical
Fixes with the pull_request trigger for untrusted builds, a separate workflow_run deploy job, the title passed through an env variable, and least-privilege permissions
Notes action pinning to a commit SHA as hardening, not a vulnerability

evals.expected_output: Leads with a Critical finding: verification fails open when the X-Signature header is absent, so any unauthenticated caller can POST a payment.succeeded event and mark any order as paid (CWE-345 or CWE-347; Likelihood High × Impact High for money). Also reports: the HMAC is computed over JSON.stringify of the parsed body rather than the raw bytes, which breaks on legitimate deliveries and pushes teams to disable verification; no replay protection (X-Timestamp is ignored and the event id isn't deduped), so a captured delivery can be replayed (CWE-294); non-constant-time comparison with !== (lower severity); and acting on the payload's orderId and type without re-fetching the payment from the provider. Fix: express.raw for this route, reject a missing or malformed signature, check a signed timestamp within a short tolerance, compare with crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, dedupe on event id with a unique constraint, and re-fetch authoritative payment state before updating the order. Each finding has severity reasoning and a regression test (for example, a request with no signature header gets 401).
expectations: Leads with a critical finding: verification fails open when X-Signature is absent, so anyone can mark an order paid
Reports the HMAC computed over JSON.stringify of the parsed body instead of the raw bytes
Reports missing replay protection: the timestamp is ignored and the event id isn't deduped
Reports the non-constant-time !== comparison at lower severity, and acting on the payload without re-fetching the payment
Fixes with express.raw, rejecting missing signatures, a signed-timestamp tolerance, crypto.timingSafeEqual, dedupe on event id, and re-fetching state
Gives a regression test, for example a request with no signature header gets 401

evals.expected_output: Reports SSRF as Likely, not Confirmed: any signed-in user controls the destination, nothing checks the resolved IP, and the default client follows redirects, but the impact depends on deployment facts outside the code. The finding states the exact checks someone must run, such as whether a pod of this service can reach the instance metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254) and whether it requires session tokens (IMDSv2 with a hop limit that blocks pods), and whether NetworkPolicies allow egress to cluster-internal and RFC 1918 ranges; these also appear under 'Needs runtime or deployment verification'. Notes that the response leaks the page title, the status line, and error text (err.Error()), which makes the SSRF partly readable and helps port scanning. Gives a conditional severity with reasons (for example High if metadata or internal services are reachable, lower if egress is locked down). Fix: a net.Dialer Control function that rejects private, loopback, link-local, and metadata addresses at connect time, a CheckRedirect that blocks or re-validates each hop, and generic error messages. Credits the existing timeout and size limit as mitigations rather than reporting them.
expectations: Reports SSRF as Likely, not Confirmed, because impact depends on deployment facts outside the code
Names the exact checks to run: whether pods reach 169.254.169.254, IMDSv2 hop-limit settings, and NetworkPolicy egress to internal ranges
Lists those checks under Needs runtime or deployment verification
Notes that the response leaks the page title, status line, and error text, which helps an attacker read responses and scan ports
Gives a conditional severity with reasons, and a fix with a dialer Control function, a CheckRedirect, and generic errors
Credits the existing timeout and size limit as mitigations
